claim: Split keyboards utilize two separate controllers where each handles a matrix half and communicates via serial or I2C over interconnect cables like TRRS.
excerpt: Many keyboards in the QMK Firmware repo are "split" keyboards. They use two controllers—one plugging into USB, and the second connected by a serial or an I2C connection over a TRRS or similar cable.

claim: Implementing I2C split interconnect requires four conductors for GND, VCC, SCL, and SDA plus 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors, necessitating a TRRS cable over 3-wire TRS.
excerpt: If you want to use I2C to communicate between halves, you will need a cable with at least 4 wires and 2x 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors.

claim: Inserting or removing TRRS or TRS cables while power is supplied can short power rails to data pins and permanently damage microcontroller boards.
excerpt: Many popular cables, in particular, TRRS/TRS cables, can cause irreparable damage to controllers if they are inserted or removed when power is already present on them.

claim: Split keyboard hand configuration can be stored in persistent EEPROM storage so the controller identifies its left or right side independently at startup.
excerpt: This method sets the keyboard's handedness by setting a flag in the persistent storage (EEPROM). This is checked when the controller first starts up, and determines what half the keyboard is

claim: The PJ-320A through-hole 3.5mm jack is the standard TRRS connector footprint used across popular open-source split keyboards.

source.title: Sofle Keyboard Build Guide RGB — GitHub

excerpt: 2 TRRS connectors PJ-320A. The same type which is used for Corne, Lily58 etc.

claim: The Nordic nRF52840 MCU and Pro Micro-compatible BLE modules like SuperMini NRF52840 are the standard drop-in choices for wireless custom keyboards.
excerpt: SuperMini NRF52840 - they are cheaper and better than nRFMicro. Buy two 301230 batteries - they fit under the controller and last for weeks.

claim: A 301230 LiPo battery (100mAh capacity) fits beneath controller socket pins and powers BLE split peripherals for approximately two weeks.
excerpt: 301230 batteries - they fit under the controller and last for weeks. ... What's the battery life? A. 2 weeks on a 100 mAh battery

claim: Integrated BLE keyboard controllers feature linear LiPo charger ICs like the TP4054 operating at 100mA charge current connected to RAW and GND pins.
excerpt: Charger: 100 mA 3.6V (TP4054), uses RAW and GND pins (same as B+/B-), voltage level on P0.04.

claim: JST PH 2.0 2-pin connectors are standard for keyboard LiPo batteries, but third-party battery leads frequently swap pin polarity relative to board standards.

source.title: Why Adafruit Feather Is So Good for Battery-Powered Prototypes — OpenELAB

excerpt: Because many cheap third-party packs use the same JST-PH 2.0 ... polarity compared with the Adafruit wiring standard.

claim: USB-C female receptacles on keyboard PCBs require dual 5.1kΩ pull-down resistors on CC1 and CC2 pins to ground for power negotiation over USB-C to USB-C cables.

source.title: USB-C Breakout Board Dual 5.1K CC1/CC2 — Amazon

excerpt: Female USB-C, dual 5.1K CC1/CC2 ... resistor to GND to enable power to go through the USB-C receptacle.

claim: Mid-mount USB-C connectors such as the HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 sit inside a PCB cutout to reduce total board-to-connector thickness.
In ZMK split firmware, the central half processes keymaps, layers, and USB/BLE host communications, while peripheral halves only send raw key and sensor events.
excerpt: In split keyboards running ZMK, one part is assigned the "central" role which receives key position and sensor events from the other parts that are called "peripherals." The central runs the necessary keymap logic to convert received events into HID events

claim: BLE-based split communication in ZMK adds an average latency of 3.75ms with a worst-case increase of 7.5ms over wired connections.
excerpt: For the currently used BLE-based transport, split communication increases the average latency by 3.75ms with a worst case increase of 7.5ms.

claim: ZMK's full-duplex wired split transport requires two dedicated UART wires connecting the halves, unlike single-wire half-duplex setups.
excerpt: Full-duplex UART requires the use of two wires connecting the halves. Future half-duplex (single-wire) UART support, which is planned, will allow using wired ZMK with designs such as the Corne, Sweep, etc. that use only a single GPIO pin for bidirectional communication between split sides.

claim: QMK split keyboards require matching microcontroller families on both halves because AVR and ARM use incompatible serial drivers and voltage levels.
excerpt: Both sides must use the same MCU family, for eg two Pro Micro-compatible controllers or two Blackpills. Currently, mixing AVR and ARM is not possible as ARM vs AVR uses different method for serial communication
